sources.locator: §6.12, printed pp. 115–118 (PDF pp. 131–134), and Appendix D.1–D.2, printed pp. 439–443 (PDF pp. 455–459), read in the extracted full text; figures and exercises excluded

contents.name: §6.12, equations (6.32)–(6.33): the cosine matrix, the form $B_M(e_i,e_j)=-\cos(\pi/m_{ij})$, and the reflections $\rho_i(x)=x-2B_M(e_i,x)e_i$
Lemma 6.12.3 (printed p. 117): the order of $\rho_i\rho_j$ is $m_{ij}$, proved by a rotation through $2\pi/m$ in the finite case and by $(\rho_i\rho_j)^n(e_i)=2nu+e_i$, $u=e_i+e_j$, for $m=\infty$
Corollary 6.12.4 (printed p. 117): the relators are sent to the identity, so $s_i\mapsto\rho_i$ extends to a homomorphism $\rho:W\to\mathrm{GL}(\mathbb R^I)$
Definition 6.12.5 (printed p. 118): the canonical representation $\rho$
Corollary 6.12.6 (printed p. 118): $(W,S)$ is a Coxeter system and the $s_i$ are distinct of order 2
contents.reason: Distinctness of the simple generators and the recognition that the presented group is a Coxeter system are not claimed on this page; the exchange-and-faithfulness page of this run proves them from its own signed-action data.

contents.name: Proposition 6.12.7 (printed p. 118): for irreducible $(W,S)$, every proper $W$-stable subspace of $\mathbb R^I$ lies in the radical of $B_M$
contents.reason: The pair proves no irreducibility or radical-containment theorem for the canonical representation, and neither page nor any of its consumers uses such a statement.

contents.name: Appendix D.1, printed pp. 439–440: the dual (geometric) representation $\rho^*$, its reflection formula (D.1), and the cone $C=\{e_i\ge0\}$ with interior $\mathring C$
Theorem D.1.1 and Corollary D.1.2 (printed p. 440): Tits' theorem $w\mathring C\cap\mathring C\ne\varnothing\Rightarrow w=1$ and faithfulness of $\rho$
contents.reason: Faithfulness of the canonical representation is the promised conclusion of the next page of this run, which carries the root-sign and half-space route; this page asserts neither positivity nor faithfulness.

contents.name: Lemma D.1.5 and its proof (printed p. 441): Property (P) in rank two, Case 1 $m=\infty$ via the affine line of the dual basis and Case 2 $m<\infty$ via positivity of $B_M$ and the sector of angle $\pi/m$
Example D.2.1(i) (printed p. 442): for $D_\infty$ the affine line $x_1+x_2=1$ is stable and the Tits cone is the half-plane $x_1+x_2\ge0$
§D.2, printed pp. 442–443 (read through Lemma D.2.3): the Tits cone $U=\bigcup_w wC$, its interior $I$, and the chamber-side and interior lemmas
contents.reason: This page computes only the rank-two chamber picture; the general Tits cone, its convexity, properness, stabilisers and chamber adjacency are the subject of the run's Tits-cone page.

contents.name: §6.12, printed p. 117: the displayed $m=\infty$ computation $(\rho_i\rho_j)^n(e_i)=2nu+e_i$
Appendix D.1, printed p. 441, Case 2: the positive definite rank-two Gram matrix with determinant $\sin^2(\pi/m)>0$

contents.name: §1.2, Example 1.2.7 (printed pp. 7–8): the dihedral group generated by two reflections, with $r_1r_2$ a rotation through $2\pi/m$ and $(r_1r_2)^m=e$

§4.2, (4.9)–(4.14) and (4.17)–(4.18) (printed pp. 93–94): the pairing $\langle p\mid\beta\rangle$, the form $(\alpha_s\mid\alpha_{s'})=-k_{s,s'}/2$, and $\sigma_s(\beta)=\beta-2(\alpha_s\mid\beta)\alpha_s$
§4.2, (4.21) (printed p. 97): the standard geometric representation $(\alpha_s\mid\alpha_{s'})=-\cos(\pi/m(s,s'))$
§4.2, Proposition 4.2.1 (printed p. 93): $\sigma_s^2=\mathrm{id}$ and the order of $\sigma_s\sigma_{s'}$ is $m(s,s')$
§4.2, Theorem 4.2.2 (printed p. 94): the map $s\mapsto\sigma_s$ has a unique extension to $\sigma:W\to\mathrm{GL}(V)$
§4.2, Proposition 4.2.3 (printed p. 94): the contragredient identity $\langle w(p)\mid\beta\rangle=\langle p\mid w^{-1}(\beta)\rangle$
§4.2, Lemma 4.2.4 through Theorem 4.2.7 (printed pp. 94–97): positivity of $w(\alpha_s)$ against length, and injectivity of $\sigma$ and $\sigma^*$
contents.reason: Positivity and faithfulness are not claimed by this pair; the run's canonical-roots page owns the root-sign and faithfulness route that consumes these results.

contents.name: §4.9 (printed p. 123): the fundamental chamber $C=\bigcap_s H^+_{\alpha_s}$, the Tits cone $U=\bigcup_w w(C)$ and the chambers $w(C)$, stated as a sketch
contents.reason: The passage is an explicit sketch of the general theory, and the general Tits-cone chamber development belongs to the run's Tits-cone page rather than to this rank-two page.

contents.name: §4.2, (4.11) (printed p. 93): $(\alpha_s\mid\alpha_s)=1$, so reflection normals are non-isotropic basis vectors

contents.name: §1.1 (printed p. 10): the Coxeter matrix convention $m_{s,s}=1$, $m_{s,s'}=m_{s',s}\ge2$, and the group presented by $(ss')^{m_{s,s'}}=1$

§1.3, Proposition 1.3 and its proof (printed p. 11): $\sigma_s(e_{s'})=e_{s'}+2\cos(\pi/m_{s,s'})e_s$, the characteristic polynomial $X^2-2\cos(2\pi/m)X+1$, exact order $m$, and infinite order for $m=\infty$
§1.11 (printed p. 14): the invariant symmetric form $(e_s,e_{s'})=-\cos(\pi/m_{s,s'})$ preserved by every $\sigma(w)$
§1.4–§1.5, Corollary 1.4 and Proposition 1.5 (printed pp. 11–12): the dihedral word structure and the signed reflection action $U_s(\epsilon,t)=(\epsilon(-1)^{\delta_{s,t}},sts)$
contents.reason: The dihedral word count and the signed action belong to the exchange-and-reduced-word page of this run, which builds them as its own items (HH-11); this page does not re-prove them.
